production.waterSource: The distillery draws mineral-rich water from the Glassaugh Spring on Durne Hill above the site.
production.malt: Core production is unpeated, with separate periods of peated production; established specialist data records peated malt above 30 ppm for those runs.
production.fermentation: Six washbacks are used, four wooden and two stainless steel. Established specialist data records a minimum fermentation of approximately 60 hours.
production.stills: A single pair of copper pot stills is used, one wash still and one spirit still, both with boil-ball geometry and vertical shell-and-tube condensation.
production.peat: Predominantly unpeated production with separately scheduled peated runs.
production.maturation: Whisky matures in coastal warehouses overlooking Sandend Bay, with bourbon, sherry, Manzanilla, port and other cask types used across the range.

houseCharacter: Mineral-rich spring water and a mixed wood/stainless fermentation setup support a ripe, fruity fermentation profile before distillation through a single pair of boil-ball stills. The distillery's standard spirit is unpeated and fruit-led, with separate peated campaigns adding a darker smoky dimension without replacing the core style. Coastal warehousing and broad cask use then reinforce Glenglassaugh's combination of tropical fruit, honeyed sweetness and maritime salinity.
cask23Narrative: Glenglassaugh sits almost on the edge of Sandend Bay, and its production is unusually easy to read in the glass: ripe fruit from fermentation and distillation, then a distinct coastal maturation environment. A single pair of boil-ball stills gives the distillery a relatively focused spirit profile, while separate peated runs create a second, smokier register without changing the identity of the core whisky. For customers, Glenglassaugh is a strong example of how location, spirit shape and cask choice can combine to create a recognisably coastal malt without relying on heavy peat alone.
